A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Polychromic Objectives for Reinforcement Learning. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite retypesetting and changed pagination.

before.justification: v4 reports original BabyAI, MiniGrid, and Triangle Discovery experiments, including performance, diversity, pass@k, and initial-state perturbation results.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–2, Figures 2–4, and the generalization material in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The polychromic objective, vine sampling, shared set advantages, GAE updates, KL penalty, and advantage window are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 specify the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same BabyAI tasks, MiniGrid FourRooms, and Algorithmic Creativity Triangle Discovery, including the same initial-state perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the pretrained policy, REINFORCE, PPO, and their reported UCB comparisons. Figures 2 and 4 retain the same Triangle Discovery comparator set.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and Appendices A–B retain the same splits, configurations, rollout counts, metrics, rewards, trajectory budgets, and hyperparameters. The perturbation protocol still samples ten starting positions per visited room.

E4.justification: The UCB comparisons, pass@k analyses, initial-state robustness evaluation, and Figure 6 trajectory case study are retained without added or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 reports averaging over three random seeds in both versions. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices are added or changed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–4 retain the same empirical values and curves. For example, Poly-PPO's Goto reward/success remains (0.575, 80.2), and its perturbed-start Goto pass rate remains 60.6%.

T1.justification: Proposition 5.5 changes each selected action's probability from p to p/n, retaining 0<p<1/n, and multiplies the displayed bound q p^n(1-p)/n by [1-(1-1/n)^n]. Appendix C.5 revises its proof using sampling with replacement and indicator variables. Appendix C.3 corrects C(theta) to use individual-action probabilities instead of joint-set probabilities and specifies lambda=alpha I(a_1:n) and lambda'=alpha n. These are localized mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about set RL, polychromic PPO, diverse successful behaviors, coverage, and robustness.

C2.justification: The interpretations of diversity, entropy collapse, and the validity–exploration tradeoff remain unchanged. The same limitations concerning environment resets, vine coverage, diversity functions, and Monte Carlo variance are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same architecture descriptions, data preparation, sampling instructions, pseudocode, and Table 3 hyperparameters. No implementation or code/data-access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prior exploration, diversity, and policy-gradient approaches are unchanged. Bibliographic typography differences do not change the referenced research.

P1.justification: Appendix C.3 gains a coefficient explanation, and C.5 gains explanatory paragraphs about sampling and indicator variables. Main-text wording, terminology, and section order otherwise remain substantially identical.

P2.justification: v6 adopts a Times-style typeface and changes title styling, wrapping, and float placement. Figure 5 moves before Appendix A.1, and Table 3 follows Algorithm 2. The figure graphics and table row/column structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected covariance term and explicit coefficients in C.3 improve mathematical precision. C.5 also addresses repeated sampling when revising Proposition 5.5, replacing v4's unexplained conditional value q/n with a fuller argument. These are limited gains: empirical evidence is unchanged, and the revised expected-diversity calculation still does not account for Section 5's special zero-diversity treatment of homogeneous samples.
